title: ICE Returns Indian National to Oregon Jail to Face Manslaughter Trial Over Fatal Crash
excerpt: Rajinder Kumar, 32, has been indicted on two counts of first-degree manslaughter over a November 2025 crash that killed William Micah Carter and Jennifer Lynn Lower. The charges are pending and have not been tested at trial.
body:
• US Immigration and Customs Enforcement has transferred Rajinder Kumar, a 32-year-old Indian national, to Oregon state custody in Deschutes County to face prosecution over a November 2025 tractor-trailer crash that killed two people.
  • Kumar has been indicted on two counts of first-degree manslaughter and three counts of recklessly endangering another person. The charges are pending in Oregon state court and have not been established at trial.
  • The Department of Homeland Security has named the victims as William Micah Carter and Jennifer Lynn Lower, who had been married for 16 days at the time of the crash.
  • For readers following the case: the state criminal case comes first — ICE says deportation proceedings will stay on hold and it will pursue Kumar's immigration case only after the state proceedings conclude.

US Immigration and Customs Enforcement has returned Rajinder Kumar, a 32-year-old Indian national, to Oregon state custody to face trial on manslaughter and reckless-endangerment charges over a highway crash that killed a newlywed couple, the agency said in an October 15 statement. ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations Seattle office transferred Kumar to face prosecution in Deschutes County, and confirmed the transfer again in a post on X on Sunday, October 18, according to the Times of India.

Kumar has been indicted in Deschutes County on two counts of first-degree manslaughter and three counts of recklessly endangering another person, ICE said. The charges stem from a November 2025 tractor-trailer accident and remain pending in Oregon state court. They are allegations that have not been established at trial.

The Crash

According to the Department of Homeland Security, on November 24, 2025, Kumar jackknifed his semi-truck and trailer, blocking both lanes of US Highway 20 in Deschutes County. A Subaru Outback collided with the semi-truck, killing the driver, William Micah Carter, and the passenger, Jennifer Lynn Lower. DHS said the couple had been married for just 16 days.

https://x.com/ICEgov/status/2111916534318686430

"Two Americans lost their lives, and their families deserve accountability. ICE worked closely with law-enforcement partners to ensure Kumar is returned to state custody to answer for the serious charges against him," said ICE ERO Seattle acting Field Office Director Julio S. Hernandez. Neither the ICE statement nor the DHS statement included a statement from Kumar or from a lawyer representing him.

The Detainer Dispute and Re-Arrest

Following Kumar's indictment, ICE lodged an immigration detainer with the Deschutes County Jail. In April 2026, Deschutes County released Kumar from custody without honouring the detainer, ICE said. DHS put the release date at April 2, 2026.

ICE officers then located and arrested Kumar on April 22, 2026, according to the DHS announcement carried by EIN Presswire. He was held at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma and placed in removal proceedings before this month's transfer back to Oregon state custody.

Kumar's Immigration History, as Stated by ICE

According to ICE, US Border Patrol apprehended Kumar near Lukeville, Arizona, on November 28, 2022, after he entered the United States from Mexico without inspection. He was placed in removal proceedings. ICE said a pending application does not confer legal status in the United States. DHS said California issued Kumar a commercial driver's licence and that the federal government had issued him work authorisation — claims DHS made while criticising California's licensing practices and the county's decision to release him.

What Happens Next

The manslaughter case will now proceed in Oregon state court in Deschutes County, where Kumar will answer the indictment. No trial date was given in the ICE or DHS statements. Federal immigration action is sequenced behind the criminal case: ICE said deportation proceedings will remain on hold until the state case concludes, and that "following the conclusion of state criminal proceedings, ICE will pursue Kumar's immigration case consistent with federal law."
